messages.subject: plyr, .parallel, .progress, R gui 2.12.2
parts:
Hi all,

In R 2.12.2, one can register/use a parallel backend in R gui. plyr
supports the parallel backend using .parallel.

I doubt that its recommended to use .progress alongside .parallel, but
in R term that just mean that the text progress bar goes till
(100/cores)%. Which is useful enough as I know how many cores there
are in the machine. With R gui, I find that if I do some thing like

## code start
## post loading libraries and registering back end

ddply(baseball, .(year), "nrow", .parallel=TRUE)

## code end

then I am fine. But,

## code start

ddply(baseball, .(year), "nrow", .parallel=TRUE, .progress="text")

## code end

hangs indefinitely in R gui (still works as "expected" in R term, bar
goes to 50%.)

I am not particularly advocating fixing .progress (I have no idea how
much work that would take). Its nice to be able to guesstimate how
long a break one can take ... waiting for the code to get done. But
not essential.

But it would be nice to quit gracefully (or ignore one of the flags)
if both flags are called in R gui. Maybe a simple fix is to always
ignore one of the flags if both are called. I know I spent a while
trying to work out why my code was hanging and then finally realized
that turning off the progress flag fixed things.

Just a thought.

Best,
Anirban
